about.lead: Plain answers about your data, the program and the rules. If anything is unclear, ask HR L&D.

privacy.title: Who sees what
privacy.intro: The Hub records your answers and scores so you can see your progress and the program can get better. Here is everyone who can see them.
privacy.you: Everything: your scores, your answers when you review them, your baseline result, your streak and your progress.
privacy.director: Your individual results, to run the program, spot where help is needed and prepare the forums. HR L&D also issues and resets PINs.
privacy.manager: Only passed or not yet for each checkpoint, and whether you have done the baseline. Never your scores or answers.
privacy.team: Averages by course and role group, only for groups of 3 people or more. Managers are never counted in team views.
privacy.nobody: No colleague sees your results. There are no rankings or leaderboards, and the Hub never shows another person's name or score.
privacy.where: Your results live in a private Google Sheet owned by the Planning Director and shared only with HR L&D. The Hub's code is public, but it holds no names, codes or scores.

leaderboards.title: Why there are no leaderboards
leaderboards.p1: Learning needs room to be wrong. A checkpoint you don't pass the first time is useful information, not a ranking.
leaderboards.p2: Leaderboards reward people who are already ahead and quietly push others to stop trying. We would rather everyone compares themselves with last week: that is the whole idea of 1% better.
leaderboards.p3: So the Hub shows your own progress, your streak and the team's averages, and nothing that ranks one colleague against another.

how.title: How the program works
how.intro: Ten courses in 2027. Each runs as a six-week cycle in four parts, and each channel does one job.
how.blink_body: 6–9 short animated episodes of 4–7 minutes, English voice with Vietnamese subtitles, on your phone or laptop.
how.hub_body: Predict before you watch, the checkpoint after, and quick recall on day 2, 7 and 30.
how.forum_body: A 4-hour offline session in Vietnamese with the Planning Director: a team case on our own data.
how.field_body: The field assignment at the S&OP step the course serves, signed off by your manager within a week.
how.r_w1_body: Do Predict, then watch the episodes on Blink.
how.r_w2_body: 10 questions; 8 of 10 and you are ready for the forum.
how.r_forum_body: Show-and-tell, the most-missed ideas, a team case and your field assignment.
how.r_w4_body: Use it on live work; your manager signs it off with the rubric.
how.r_recall_body: Three quick questions each time, so it sticks.
how.sessions_body: About every six weeks, on a Tuesday afternoon after S&OP sign-off. Pitch Day and the War Room take the place of a forum.

rules.intro: The same rules for everyone, applied by the Hub.
rules.predict_body: 3 questions before the videos. Ungraded and unlimited, and you see the answers straight away. Guessing first helps you remember.
rules.checkpoint: Checkpoint: the gate to the forum
rules.checkpoint_body: 10 questions from one of two parallel forms. Pass mark 80% (8 of 10). An unanswered question counts as wrong.
rules.retake_body: Not yet? Retake 24 hours after your last try, with the other form.

rules.late_body: If you haven't passed when the checkpoint closes, still come to the forum. You can finish in the week after, with your manager.

rules.recall_body: After you pass: 3 questions on day 2, 7 and 30 after the forum, from the form you didn't take. It doesn't affect the gate.
rules.baseline_body: 60 minutes, one attempt, 16–27 Nov 2026. The same test again 29 Nov – 10 Dec 2027 shows how far you have come. No pass mark.
rules.pitch_body: Your team project: Pitch Day on 22 Jun 2027 (the mid-point) and the capstone S&OP War Room on 21 Dec 2027, scored by a panel on a five-criterion rubric.

faq.title: Questions
faq.q1: Can my manager see my score?
faq.q1_a: No. Your manager sees only passed or not yet for each checkpoint, and whether you have done the baseline.
faq.q2: What happens if I don't pass the checkpoint?
faq.q2_a: Nothing bad. You see what to revisit, rewatch those episodes and retake after 24 hours with the other form. A third try opens after a short chat with your manager.
faq.q3: Why can't I see the right answers yet?
faq.q3_a: So the other form stays a fair test. You see your own answers and the ideas to revisit straight away; the right answers appear once you pass, or a week after the forum.
faq.q4: I missed the checkpoint deadline. What now?
faq.q4_a: Come to the forum anyway. The checkpoint stays open for a week after the forum so you can finish it with your manager. After that, your manager can unlock one more try.
faq.q5: Does the Hub know which videos I watched?
faq.q5_a: No. Blink doesn't share that. You tick episodes yourself on the course page; it only helps you keep track.
faq.q6_a: Yes. Every page works on a phone. For the 60-minute baseline, a laptop and a quiet hour make it easier.
faq.q7_a: Yes. Use EN | VI at the top of any page. Questions and answers switch too, and your choice is remembered.
faq.q8: What are the streak and the 1% meter?
faq.q8_a: Your streak counts the weeks in a row you did something on the Hub. The meter shows 1.01 to the power of your active weeks: 52 active weeks make 1.68×. Only you see it.
faq.q9: Who do I contact for help?
faq.q9_a: HR L&D for PINs, access and Blink. Your manager for field work and sign-offs. The Planning Director for anything about the content.

rubric.title: How the panel scores
rubric.intro: Each judge scores 1–5 on five criteria. These are the anchors for 1, 3 and 5.
rubric.weight_capstone: Capstone: Verified result and Value count double.

c1.name: Problem defined
c1.what: A gap in numbers, a date, a decision-maker and guard rails.
c1.a3: Gap in numbers and a date
c1.a5: Gap, date, decision-maker and guard rails; passes all six characteristics

c2.name: Structured analysis
c2.what: A MECE tree, priorities, hypotheses tested with data.
c2.a5: Hypothesis-driven tree, 80:20 focus, hypotheses tested with data, iterated

c3.name: Verified result
c3.what: KPI before and after from the system of record, held for 4 weeks or more.
c3.a3: KPI moved, from the system of record
c3.a5: KPI moved and held ≥ 4 weeks, with a clean before/after and no side effects

c4.name: Value and sustainability
c4.what: A VND basis that's agreed; the rule, process or tool change that keeps it.
c4.a5: Value agreed with Finance; a rule, process or tool change keeps it

c5.name: Communication
c5.what: Answer first, action titles, a one-page summary, handles questions.
c5.a5: One-page summary, action title on every slide, handles questions crisply
